review_notes: Source (read_long_names, libelf/elf_begin.c) is project code, not the fuzz harness wrapper (LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput at fuzz-libdwfl.c:47 is correctly kept only as the coarse-trace entry). The specific vulnerability-relevant source value `string = hdr->ar_size` at line 760 is where the untrusted, non-NUL-terminated ar_size field is taken as the pointer handed to atol.

All key line numbers verified against the vulnerable commit 1b09e67 (n132/arvo:45636-vul): line 743 `hdr = (struct ar_hdr *) (elf->map_address + offset)` (tainted_value_origin), line 760 `const char *string = hdr->ar_size` (source), line 761 `if (hdr->ar_size[sizeof (hdr->ar_size) - 1] != ' ')` (bounds_state / NUL-termination lifetime), line 766 `len = atol (string)` (sink & root_cause). All match exactly.

root_cause is supported by patch.diff: the fix inserts `if (!isdigit(string[0])) return NULL;` immediately before `len = atol (string);` (patch commit ed42e7cf, ChangeLog 'Check ar_size starts with a digit'). The GT root_cause.description explains the concrete mechanism (space-padded last byte => no NUL-terminated stack-buf copy is made => `string` keeps pointing at raw mmap'd bytes => atol with no digit scans past the mapping) rather than 'the crash disappears'. Faithful.

tainted_value_origin (hdr aliased onto mmap at 743) is distinct from source (string at 760) and correctly identifies the first materialization of attacker bytes inside read_long_names; the depends_on data edges 1->2->3->5->6 form a coherent data/control-flow trace, not a call stack.
parser_admitted (__libelf_next_arhdr_wrlock long-name dispatch) is a genuine earlier format-acceptance point (input admitted ELF_K_AR, member name second byte isdigit) distinct from the sink at 766.

Reclassification from the OSS-Fuzz auto-tag CWE-190/191/680 to CWE-125 out-of-bounds-read is justified: the observed ASan fault is a wild-pointer READ of size 985 inside __interceptor_atol (sink matches crash frame #1 at elf_begin.c:766), i.e. an out-of-bounds read, not an integer overflow. The normalized description documents this reconciliation.

Minor (cosmetic, no fix required): reachability_checkpoints.parser_admitted.code uses the line-913 continuation fragment '&& read_long_names (elf) == NULL))' while anchoring line 912. The `if (unlikely (...))` statement spans lines 912-913 and the ASan stack authoritatively attributes frame #2 to line 912, so the 912 anchor is correct and consistent; the fine_trace step 1 for the same site uses the full statement text.
No bootstrap/first-pass wording present in final GT fields.
